_doc: Events that belong to the whole subject. Course histories carry the rest.

milestones.title: Kepler’s first two laws
milestones.detail: Johannes Kepler’s Astronomia Nova stated that planets move on ellipses with the Sun at one focus, and that a line from the Sun to a planet sweeps equal areas in equal times.

milestones.title: Kepler’s third law
milestones.detail: In Harmonices Mundi Kepler published the relation between a planet’s period and the size of its orbit, which Newton later derived from the inverse-square law.

milestones.title: Weighing the Earth
milestones.detail: Henry Cavendish measured the gravitational attraction between lead spheres with a torsion balance and so determined the mean density of the Earth, and with it G.

milestones.title: A finite speed of light
milestones.detail: Ole Rømer explained the irregular timing of Jupiter’s moons by a finite speed of light, the first measurement of that speed.

milestones.title: Cosmic rays
milestones.detail: Victor Hess, carrying electroscopes on balloon flights, found that the ionisation of air increases with altitude. The radiation comes from outside the Earth.

milestones.title: The Hubble law
milestones.detail: Edwin Hubble reported that the redshifts of galaxies are proportional to their distances. The relation is the first evidence that the universe expands.

milestones.title: The cosmic microwave background
milestones.detail: Arno Penzias and Robert Wilson found an excess antenna temperature of about 3 K, identified by Dicke, Peebles, Roll and Wilkinson as the cooled radiation of a hot early universe.

milestones.title: Accelerated expansion
milestones.detail: Two teams measuring distant type Ia supernovae found that the expansion of the universe is speeding up, now described by a cosmological constant.

milestones.title: A black hole, imaged
milestones.detail: The Event Horizon Telescope published an image of the ring of emission around the black hole in the galaxy M87, on the scale of the photon orbit.
